messages:
Naomi Rivera: Idea: prompt-segment-aware precision (PSAP) - use different precision for different semantic segments of the prompt + generation (system, instruction, code blocks, user convo). Goal: keep perf wins but avoid quality loss where it matters (e.g., code, facts).
Carlos Mendes: interesting. How do we detect segments reliably and cheaply in runtime?
Naomi Rivera: classifier on the prompt at request time (fast regex+ML hybrid). tag spans: system, user, instruction, code, citation. Produce a small bitmask: e.g., seg=SYS|CODE|USER.
Ivy Park: runtime cost concern: extra parsing/classification per request adds latency. proposal: do classification only at route level for requests > N tokens or enable sampling. cheap fallback: rely on explicit header from SDK (clients can mark code blocks).
Naomi Rivera: good point. SDK hinting is primary, classifier secondary. also cache classification for repeating prompts per-tenant.
Carlos Mendes: how does precision map to segments? e.g., keep CODE and SYSTEM at int8, USER at fp8 or 4bit? That seems backwards.
Naomi Rivera: sketch mapping: safety/fact/code segments -> higher fidelity (int8 or fp8 with calibration), creative/user chit-chat -> lower precision (4bit) where acceptable. Also KV cache policy: store keys in high precision for code segments to avoid generation drift.
Ivy Park: KV storage in higher precision increases memory. need to trade memory vs correctness. maybe only cache higher-precision for last-K tokens of code spans.
Naomi Rivera: yes add per-segment kv_ttl and kv_precision. default kv_precision: code=fp8,k=fp8 ; user=4bit; kv_ttl: code=512 tokens, user=64.
Carlos Mendes: evaluation: how do we prove this improves unit-cost without hurting quality?
Naomi Rivera: plan: A/B shadowing. route a small % to PSAP and measure anchor diffs on segment-specific anchor sets: code anchors, factual QA anchors, conversational anchors. metrics: topk-kl, human eval on code exec pass rate, factual accuracy.
Ivy Park: telemetry: per-segment counters (requests, avg_latency, fallback_rate, kv_miss), but sample only 0.5% detailed traces. avoid high-cardinality by aggregating over segment types.
Carlos Mendes: what about safety/privacy? classification could leak PII to classifier model. Must run classifier locally in-service and avoid sending segments to other services.
Naomi Rivera: agreed. Classifier must be deterministic regex-first and then tiny on-host model. No external network calls. Add opt-out: tenant can force-disable classifier and rely on SDK hints.
Ivy Park: rollout plan?
Naomi Rivera: step 0: offline simulation on historical prompts to label segments and compute projected savings + risk. step 1: internal shadow (0.5%) with sampling and anchor checks for code/facts. step 2: 5% canary with auto-fallback disabled. step 3: 25% with auto-fallback and per-segment limits. step 4: global if stable. Gate each step on segment-anchor thresholds.
Carlos Mendes: runtime flags needed: psap_enabled, classifier_mode(regex|ml|off), per_segment_map, kv_precision_defaults.
Ivy Park: add lint: block profiles that map safety_critical segments to <int8 without two-person signoff.
Naomi Rivera: ops-bot: create ticket ML-4991 for PSAP eval+rollout?
ops-bot: Created ML-4991: "Prompt-segment-aware precision (PSAP) rollout checklist" assigned to Naomi Rivera, Carlos Mendes, Ivy Park. https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-4991 :white_check_mark:
Carlos Mendes: action items: 1) Naomi: run historical prompt segmentation + savings estimate. 2) Ivy: prototype on-host classifier (regex-first). 3) Carlos: build anchor sets for code+factual segments and integrate into eval harness.
Ivy Park: timeline: prototype classifier in 2 weeks, historical sim this week, shadow canary target in 3 weeks if sims look good.
Naomi Rivera: thanks all. Also note: expose a per-tenant override header so enterprise customers can opt-in/opt-out easily.
Carlos Mendes: let's be careful with metrics; include per-segment quality quotas in the profile so auto-fallback respects them.
Ivy Park: agreed. final note: document privacy and classifier internals in internal runbook before shadowing.
Naomi Rivera: will draft the runbook and update ML-4991. thanks :thumbsup:
